records.title: National Optical Fibre Network Policy
details:
(a) whether Government plans to formulate a National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN) Policy, if so, the details thereof;

(b) whether Government plans to adopt uniform Right of Way (RoW) measures for greater involvement of States in the policy;

(c) whether Government plans to release more spectrum for successful rollout of wireless broadband, ensuring seamless execution of the NOFN policy; and

(d) whether Government plans to connect Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to National Internet Exchange of India (NIXI), making it an effective Internet Exchange Point (IXP), if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
(SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD)

(a) & (b) National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN) was planned, in 2011, to connect all the 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) in the country through optical fibre utilizing existing fibres of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) viz. Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL), RailTel and Power Grid and laying incremental fibre wherever necessary to bridge the connectivity gap between Gram Panchayats and Blocks, for providing broadband connectivity by all categories of service providers on non-discriminatory basis. The project is being executed by a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) namely, Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL), which has been incorporated on 25.02.2012 under Indian Companies Act 1956.

NOFN Project was envisaged as a Centre-State joint effort. State Governments are expected to contribute by way of not levying any Right of Way (RoW) charges. This requires suitable Tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to be signed by Central Government, State Governments & Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL). Tripartite MoU has been signed with all the States and Union Territories except Tamil Nadu and Lakshadweep.

(c) Spectrum available in various frequency bands for telecommunication services including wireless broadband, put for auction conducted from time to time, has increased the availability of spectrum with telecom service providers. Based on the reference made by Government, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released a Consultation paper dated 26.11.2015 on valuation and reserve price of spectrum in 700 Megahertz(MHz), 800 MHz, 900 MHz, 1800 MHz, 2100 MHz and 2500 MHz band for the next round of auction of spectrum.

(d) Government has setup National Internet Exchange of India (NIXI) nodes at various locations in the country for Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to connect. At present, 43 ISPs at 7 locations (Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Ahmedabad) are already connected with NIXI. With increasing data traffic, it is expected more number of ISPs will get connected at these NIXI nodes.

records.title: Private entities to manufacture space related equipment
details:
(a) whether Government plans to incubate private entities manufacturing space related equipments under ''Make in India'' scheme, if so, details thereof;

(b) whether Government plans to allow active collaboration between the Earth Sciences and Space Ministries for developing disaster mitigation techniques; and

(c) whether Government has carried out timely appraisals of the remote sensing data policy, if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PG & PENSIONS AND IN THE PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE
(DR. JITENDRA SINGH):

(a) ISRO is making focussed efforts to consolidate and enhance participation of Indian industries including private entities in the manufacture of space related hardware such as rocket engine & stages, propellant tanks, spacecraft structures, solar panels, thermal control systems etc., required for satellites and launch vehicles. It is envisaged that the industry will have enhanced contribution towards manufacture of standardised components as well as integrated systems /subsystems through appropriate consortium.

(b) Yes Sir. Ministry of Earth Sciences and Department of Space are collaborating for developing disaster mitigation techniques for accurate forecasting of cyclone track & intensity, heavy rainfall alerts, fog, inundation scenarios in the coastal areas and in establishment of Tsunami & Storm Surge Warning Centre and Doppler Weather Radars.

(c) Yes Sir. Taking note of advances in imaging capability with high spatial resolution, both at national and global level and prevailing security considerations, Government has carried out an appraisal of the then existing RSDP 2001 and positioned new/revised RSDP 2011 with a view to ensure availability of high resolution data for developmental purposes. RSDP 2011, permits distribution of all satellite data of resolutions up to 1 m (as compared to 5.8 m in RSDP 2001) on a non-discriminatory and “as requested basis” to the user; and all data of better than 1 m resolution after screening and clearance by the appropriate agency prior to distribution.

*****

records.title: Classification of weaker section for Housing for All scheme
details:
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:

(a) whether Government plans to establish a robust criteria for classification of weaker sections, for affordable housing, under Housing for All scheme 2022; and

(b) whether Government plans to elucidate on the mandatory conditions for easing up of urban land market for providing adequate land for affordable housing, under the same?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION
[SHRI BABUL SUPRIYO]


(a): Under the “Housing for All (Urban)” Mission launched on 25.6.2015, Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) have been defined as urban poor with annual household income upto Rs. 3 lakhs and Low Income Group (LIG) with annual household income between 3-6 lakhs.

(b): Land and Colonization are State subjects and it is for them to assess the land requirement for housing projects. Availability of urban land is, however, the biggest constraint in providing housing to all including weaker sections. In order to ease administrative bottlenecks, a set of Mandatory Conditions have been included in the “Housing for All (Urban)” Mission to facilitate growth of housing sector including affordable housing. For participating in the Mission and to avail of financial assistance from Central Government, States/ UTs should agree to fulfil Mandatory Conditions prescribed under Mission Guidelines.
******

records.title: (clubbed) STUDY ON TRAFFIC GROWTH .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) the total strength of aircrafts owned and operated by
 Indian Airlines at present;
(b) the number of aircrafts which have outlived their normal
 lives and require replacement;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government are considering a
 proposal for purchase of 43 aircrafts at a cost of Rs.10,000
 crores instead of obtaining them on wet/dry lease;
(d) whether any study on traffic growth has been undertaken
 which would justify purchase of these aircrafts instead of
 taking them on wet/dry lease; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?

MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY ) 
 (a): Indian Airlines has a fleet of 47 owned aircraft.
 (b): There is no prescribed upper age for commercial
 aircraft. However, the aircraft have a design economic life
 beyond which the operation becomes uneconomical due to the
 increasing maintenance cost.
 (c): The project report of Indian Airlines for acquisition
 of 43 aircraft at the cost of Rs.10,089 crores has since
 been received.
 (d) and (e): The working group on Civil Aviation for the
 Tenth Five Year Plan has projected average annual growth
 rate in domestic passenger traffic to be of 5% and that in
 international passenger traffic to be of 6%. 
 The new aircraft are envisaged to replace the entire fleet
 of A-300 and B-737-200 in a phased manner by March, 2005 as
 well as to cater to the projected traffic growth during the
 five year period.

records.title: PENALISING IMPACT OF SUBSIDY CUT ON PRIVATE FERTILIZER PLANTS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that heavy losses are being sustained by most of the public 
sector fertilizer plants year after year which were as high as Rs. 2,466 crore in the 
year 2001-02, as per the report of the Ministry; and
(b) whether Government are subsidizing such losses, at the same time trying to save 
much smaller amounts on subsidy, by penalizing the efficiency of private and 
cooperative sector fertilizer plants, under the garb of reducing subsidy, if so, how 
government expect to ensure continued health and viability of efficiently run 
fertilizer plants ?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)
(a): There are 8 Public Sector Undertakings under the administrative control of the 
Department of Fertilizers. Out of these, 5 companies including 4 sick companies, 
reported losses for 2001-02. The total loss reported by these companies for 2001-02 is 
Rs. 2142.48 crore. 
(b): Parameters/norms, governing the determination of subsidy payments, are applied 
uniformly to all urea manufacturing units, whether they are in private sector, public 
sector or cooperative sector.

records.title: NEW BILATERAL AGREEMENT OF AI WITH MALAYSIAN AND EMIRATES AIRLINES .
details:
(a) whether Air India has signed any new bilateral agreement
 with Emirates recently; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor?

MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV)
(a) and (b): During last round of bilateral air services
consultation between India and United Arab Emirates (Dubai)
held in Delhi on 19-20th April, 2001, Hyderabad has been
granted as an additional point of call to the designated
airline of Dubai, i.e., Emirates with a separate entitlement

declared international airport of Hyderabad. Emirates`
operations between Dubai and Hyderabad would be covered by

records.title: SUBJECT CUSTOMS DUTY ON AUDIO MAGNETIC TAPES
details:
(a)Whether it is a fact that Customs duty on inputs for 
 manufacture of Audio Magnetic Tape is 38.5 per cent whereas
 it is 20 per cent for imported finished products.;
(b) whether Government are aware that this inverted duty 
structure is gross discrimination against the domestic industry
resulting in closure of more than 50 per cent units in the last
decade and many more are on the verge of closure;
(c) whether Government have received representations from the 
 industry to bring down duty on inputs down to zero percent 
to make it competitive; and
(d) if so, what action Government propose to take to correct
 these anomalies and by when?

(a): The major inputs used in the manufacture of Audio Magnetic
Tapes are Polyester Films, Polyurethane Elastomer and Gamma 
Ferric Oxide. While the import duty on Gamma Ferric Oxide is
16.5% ad valorem (inclusive of surcharge), the import duty on
the other inputs mentioned above is 38.5% ad valorem (inclusive
of surcharge). The import duty on Audio Magnetic Tape is 20% 
ad valorem.
(b),(c) and (d): Information available with the Government for
1998 and 1999 does not indicate any decline in the production 
of audio magnetic tapes . The Government have received
representations from the industry requesting for reduction
in import duty on inputs used in the manufacture of audio 
magnetic tapes to a level of 5% ad valorem. The 
representations will be examined as part of the Budget 
exercise for the year 2001-2002.

Ministries/Departments, which have components of disaster mitigation, towards long-term 
rehabilitation measures in the wake of natural calamities.

records.title: CIVIL AVIATION POLICY .
details:
(a) whether a Draft Civil Aviation Policy is under the
 consideration of Government;
(b) if so, what are the primary objectives of the proposed
 policy and by what time the policy is likely to be
 formulated;
(c) whether it is a fact that there are serious differences
 about creation of Civil Aviation Authority;
(d) if so, the details and functions of Authority; and
(e) what would be the future role of the Directorate General
 of Civil Aviation and Bureau of Civil Aviation Security in
 the event of creation of Civil Aviation Authority.

MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV)
(a): Yes, Sir.
(b) to (e): The draft Civil Aviation Policy, seeks to set
up a policy framework to promote efficient, cost effective
and orderly growth of air transport, ensure safety and
security in accordance with international standard and
generate a healthy competitive civil aviation environment
which contribute to social and economic development of the
country. This policy document is being finalised and will
be announced in the near future.


records.title: POOR QUALITY OF SERVICE OFFERED BY AI AND IA .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian Airlines and Air India
 have accumulated losses over the years;
(b) whether it is also a fact that performance and quality
 of service to the passengers have nose-dived over the years
 and there have been mounting complaints in this regard;
(c) whether Government have been contemplating partial
 privatisation of both the airlines; and
(d) if so; the details thereof?

MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV)
(a): Yes, Sir.
(b): There is scope for improvement. Both the airlines
constantly endeavour to bring about improvements in the
services rendered to the passengers both on the ground and
in the air.
(c) & (d) :The Government has approved in principle,
bringing down the equity of the Government of India in Air
India to 40% through a process of disinvestment by sale of
40% of equity to a strategic partner, upto 10% to employees
and the balance by sale to financial institutions and/or on
the share market. In the event of the strategic partner
being a joint venture with an element of foreign holding,
the arrangement should be such as would limit foreign
holding in Air India to a maximum of 26% of the total
equity.
As regards, Indian Airlines, Government has decided to
disinvest 51 per cent of equity of Indian Airlines out of
which 26 per cent of the equity would be given to a
strategic partner who whould be given a free hand in the
management under the supervision of board of directors.
Remaining 25% of the equity would be offered to employees,
financial institutions and public.

